reasoning_audit.detail: Interest applies to opening principal with the payment-period subscript; primary spending includes transfers/investment without confusing expenditure GDP G. Financial acquisition or cash draw is separate from primary expenditure. Par issuance includes maturing principal, with noncash valuation explicitly excluded from the cash equation. Gross/net and liquidity/solvency distinctions are maintained.

reasoning_audit.area: Exact real and GDP debt dynamics
reasoning_audit.detail: Current-period GDP denominates primary flows and adjustments. The carrying factor is(1+i)/[(1+pi)(1+g)], with positive gross factors. The real-rate relation is exact before approximation. The example in which the first-order shortcut reverses the sign is arithmetically correct.

The alpha<1, alpha=1 and alpha>1 branches, fixed-surplus solution and alpha-phi feedback coefficient are correctly derived. Gross debt stops or changes regime at zero. A binding fiscal cap invalidates the uncapped closed form. The debt-capacity threshold is explicitly conditional on constant rates/growth, zero adjustments and a feasible permanent surplus bound.

Finite telescoping retains discounted terminal debt. Infinite equality requires an explicit vanishing terminal term, not just period budget balance or a bounded GDP ratio. Constant nominal S and a constant GDP share are kept distinct. The R<Gamma stationary-ratio counterexample violates the stated terminal condition without asserting a universal impossibility theorem for other debt/liquidity/overlapping-generation models.

The fixed-price slack-capacity consumption/investment/rate system is complete, with D=1-c(1-tau)+b*psi>0 for algebraic uniqueness and separate nonnegative-output/rate/capacity checks. Automatic-stabilizer comparisons preserve the initial tax burden. Equal discretionary tax/purchase changes need not preserve the realized balance. The debt-denominator effect is limited to a one-period experiment.

General financing neutrality now preserves the optimal set and requires uniqueness for a unique path. Same-household future taxes, borrowing access, rate, purchases and counterparties are explicit. The log cases have a strictly concave objective, positive consumption and checked constraint derivative signs. Aggregate transfer impact and welfare judgments are correctly separated.

Definitions precede equations; worked cases lead to transfer, boundary and critique exercises. Scenario paths carry no invented probabilities or causal multiplier interpretation. Actual primary-source claims are scoped; source projections are not inserted into synthetic examples. Every requested exercise component has an answer, including open-memo evaluation criteria.
